contentHtml:
For a small kitchen, choose an L-shape if the room is at least about 8 × 6 ft, a parallel layout if it is long and at least 7.5 ft wide, and a straight single-wall kitchen if it is under 7 ft wide. Then add storage upward with tall units and full-height wall cabinets, use drawers instead of shelves, fit a corner pull-out, and keep finishes light and handle-free. In Gurgaon, a small modular kitchen typically costs ₹3 to ₹7 lakh.

Most 2BHK and many 3BHK kitchens in Gurgaon are between 60 and 85 sq ft. That is enough for a well-run kitchen, but not for a single wasted inch. The good news is that small kitchens are where modular design works hardest. This guide covers modular kitchen designs for small kitchens: which layout fits your room, twelve ideas that add storage and space, and what it costs.

Key facts at a glance

QuestionShort answer
How big is a "small" kitchen in Gurgaon?Typically 60 to 85 sq ft in 2BHK apartments
Best layout for most small kitchens?L-shape, from about 8 × 6 ft
Narrow kitchen under 7 ft wide?Straight, single-wall kitchen
Minimum width for a parallel kitchen?About 7.5 ft (two 2 ft counters plus a 3.5 ft aisle)
Standard counter depth?2 ft (600 mm)
Cost of a small modular kitchen?About ₹3 to ₹7 lakh for a 60 to 80 sq ft kitchen

Step one: pick the layout your room allows

The room decides the layout, not the catalogue. Measure the clear width wall to wall at counter height, then use this table.

Kitchen shape and sizeLayoutWhy
Under 7 ft wideStraight (single wall)Leaves a usable aisle; two counters would not fit
About 8 × 6 ft to 10 × 8 ftL-shapeTwo counters, one open side, room to move
Long and narrow, 7.5 ft wide or moreParallelNo corners; everything one step away
Small but open to the dining areaL-shape with a breakfast counter or peninsulaExtra worktop and seating without an island

Islands rarely suit small kitchens. They need roughly 10.5 ft of clear depth and clearance on every side. Our full kitchen layout guide explains the numbers.

12 modular kitchen design ideas for small kitchens

Storage ideas

1. Go full height. Run wall cabinets up to the ceiling. The top row holds things you use a few times a year, such as festival dinnerware and spare appliances.

2. Add a tall unit. A floor-to-ceiling pantry or larder unit, 450 or 600 mm wide, holds more than several base cabinets and keeps groceries off the counter.

3. Use drawers, not shelves, below the counter. Deep drawers bring everything to you. Nothing gets lost at the back of a shelf, and a full set of pots fits in one drawer.

4. Fix the corner. In an L-shape, the corner is the least usable space. A carousel, magic corner or blind-corner pull-out turns it into working storage.

5. Use the plinth and the backsplash. Plinth drawers below the base cabinets suit trays and baking tins. A rail system on the backsplash keeps spices, ladles and towels within reach without using counter space.

6. Plan the bottle and spice pull-outs. A 150 to 200 mm pull-out beside the hob holds oils and masalas, exactly where they are used.

Space and light ideas

7. Keep finishes light. White, off-white, pale grey or light wood fronts reflect light and make the room feel larger. Use a darker colour only on the base cabinets if you want contrast.

8. Go handle-less. Profile handles, push-to-open fronts or J-pull handles keep surfaces flat and stop hips catching on handles in a narrow aisle.

9. Add under-cabinet lighting. A continuous LED strip under the wall cabinets lights the counter without shadows, which matters more in a small kitchen than any ceiling fixture.

10. Use a glossy or glass backsplash. A single sheet of toughened glass or a light, glossy tile reflects light and has fewer grout lines to clean.

Working ideas

11. Keep the work triangle tight. Sink, hob and refrigerator should each be 4 to 9 ft apart. In a small L-shape, place the sink and hob on the long arm and the refrigerator at the end near the entrance.

12. Move what you can out of the kitchen. If the flat has a utility balcony, move the washing machine, water purifier, second sink and bulk storage there. It frees the kitchen for cooking.

Small kitchens and Indian cooking

Indian cooking puts specific demands on a small kitchen. Plan for them from the start:

  • Chimney and exhaust. A ducted chimney directly above the hob, venting to the outside, matters more in a small closed kitchen, where heat and smells have nowhere else to go.
  • Counter space for prep. Keep at least an unbroken stretch of counter between the sink and the hob for chopping and grinding.
  • Tall, heavy-duty drawers. Pressure cookers, kadhais and big steel containers need deep drawers with strong channels.
  • A heat-tolerant counter. Granite tolerates hot vessels better than quartz. Our quartz vs granite guide compares the two.

Materials that work in small kitchens

ElementGood choice for a small kitchen
Cabinet carcassBWR or BWP plywood, or HDHMR, for moisture resistance near the sink
ShuttersLight acrylic, laminate or PU finishes; handle-less profiles
CountertopGranite for heavy cooking; quartz for a light, uniform look
HardwareSoft-close hinges and full-extension drawer channels
BacksplashToughened glass or light glossy tiles

For the board comparison, see our guide to plywood vs MDF vs particle board.

What does a small modular kitchen cost in Gurgaon?

Kitchen sizeEstimated cost
Small kitchen (60 to 80 sq ft)About ₹3 to ₹7 lakh
2BHK apartment kitchenAbout ₹3 to ₹8 lakh

The final figure depends on the board, shutter finish, hardware brand, countertop and the number of tall units and pull-outs. Hardware and accessories are where small kitchens get their efficiency, so this is the last place to cut. Our modular kitchen cost guide breaks the costs down further.

Five small-kitchen mistakes to avoid

  1. Choosing a layout too big for the room. A U-shape or island in a narrow kitchen leaves an aisle one person can barely use.
  2. Open shelves everywhere. They look good in photos but collect dust and grease quickly in an Indian kitchen.
  3. A corner with no pull-out. The deepest storage in the room becomes dead space.
  4. Dark, glossy finishes throughout. They make a small room feel smaller and show every fingerprint.
  5. Forgetting the chimney duct. Fix the duct route before fixing the hob position.

faqs.question: Which modular kitchen design is best for a small kitchen?
faqs.answer: An L-shape is best for most small kitchens of about 8 × 6 ft or more, because it gives two counters and keeps the floor open. For a long, narrow kitchen at least 7.5 ft wide, choose a parallel layout. Under 7 ft wide, a straight single-wall kitchen works best.

faqs.question: How can I get more storage in a small modular kitchen?
faqs.answer: Run wall cabinets to the ceiling, add a tall pantry unit, use drawers instead of shelves below the counter, fit a corner pull-out, and use plinth drawers and backsplash rails. Moving the washing machine and bulk storage to a utility balcony frees more space.

faqs.question: What colours make a small kitchen look bigger?
faqs.answer: Light colours such as white, off-white, pale grey and light wood reflect light and make a small kitchen feel larger. Pair them with handle-less shutters, under-cabinet lighting and a glossy or glass backsplash.

faqs.question: How much does a small modular kitchen cost in Gurgaon?
faqs.answer: A small modular kitchen of 60 to 80 sq ft typically costs about ₹3 to ₹7 lakh in Gurgaon. The board, shutter finish, hardware, countertop and number of pull-outs decide where in that range it lands.

faqs.question: Can a small kitchen have an island?
faqs.answer: Usually not. An island needs about 42 inches of clearance on every side, which takes roughly 10.5 ft of clear depth. In a small kitchen, a peninsula or breakfast counter attached to an L-shape gives the same seating and worktop.

faqs.question: What is the minimum size for a modular kitchen?
faqs.answer: An L-shape works from about 8 × 6 ft. A straight kitchen can work along a single wall of 7 ft or more in a narrower room. A parallel kitchen needs at least 7.5 ft of width.

faqs.question: Is a modular kitchen worth it for a small space?
faqs.answer: Yes. Small kitchens gain the most from modular design, because pull-outs, tall units and full-extension drawers make every inch accessible in a way that open shelves and fixed cupboards cannot.
